 Order

Petitioner is knocking at the doors of Writ Court for assailing the provisions of Section 3-A to 3-I of the National Highways Act, 1956, as amended, which inter alia exclude application of the provisions of erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894 inter alia for the purpose of awarding solatium and interest.

Petitioner has made the alternative prayer with the following text:
"Alternatively and in the event of this Hon'ble Court inclined to grant the reliefs at (i)
& (ii) above, the Petitioner prays that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to direct the Respondents to pay compensation to the Petitioner in respect of the portion of the schedule property in Sy.No.115 of Kannamangala Village, at the rate prevailing as on 4th week of June, 2013."
2. After service of notice, the Respondents having entered appearance through their Senior Panel Counsel, oppose the Petition inter alia contending that without the Union of India as a party, the question of constitutionality of the provisions cannot be gone into; the decision of the learned single judge of this Court in LALITA vs. UNION OF INDIA, AIR 2003 KAR 165, which has struck down Section 3-J of the 1894 Act would now pale into insignificance since W.A.Nos.6115-6117/2002 between UNION OF INDIA vs. LALITHA filed against the same has been disposed off vide judgment dated 15.10.2019 in terms of Apex Court decision in UNION OF INDIA AND ANOTHER vs.
TARSEM SINGH AND OTHERS, AIR 2019 SC 4689.

sentences.text:
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court is inclined to grant a limited indulgence in the matter as under and for the following reasons:
(a) There is force in the submission of learned counsel for the Petitioner that now in view of the Division Bench decision made in terms of Apex Court decision supra, the 1st prayer for quashment of the provisions of the 1894 Act has become infructuous and therefore, the alternate prayer is to be granted to the extent of awarding solatium and other related benefits like interest.

The Division Bench following UNION OF INDIA AND ANOTHER vs. TARSEM SINGH AND OTHERS, AIR 2019 SC 4689, has said as under:
"5.

sentences.text: When the matters were taken up today, learned counsel for the parties jointly submitted that the controversy in the instant appeals are squarely covered by an order dated 19.09.2019 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.7064/2019 namely Union of India and another vs. Tarsem Singh and others."

entities.text: Union of India and another vs. Tarsem Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (b) In view of the above declaration of law by the Apex Court in terms of which the Division Bench also has disposed off the Writ Appeal, petitioner is entitled to award of solatium as if the acquisition has been made under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
This solatium has to be computed with effect from the date the possession of property has been taken which has been the consistent view of the courts all through.

(c) The contention of the Panel counsel for the Respondent that the hearing of the case be deferred till after the Apex Court clarifies the reckoning date for computation of solatium and interest cannot be agreed with since there is no stay by the Apex Court unlike there was one when the invocability of Section 24(2) of THE Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 was being debated.
In view of the above, the Writ Petition is allowed in terms of prayer No.3 and the Respondents are directed to compute the solatium part of the compensation reckoned from the date of taking actual possession of the subject land and pay it to the Petitioner with statutory rate of interest, within a period of three months, if he establishes his credentials in accordance with law.
